title: Probability
intro: Probability from the ground up: events and their rules, random variables and the standard distributions, several variables at once, the tools and inequalities that make calculations possible, the limit theorems, random processes, inference, and the measure-theoretic foundations underneath it all.

blocks.text: Probability is the mathematics of uncertainty: it assigns numbers to events, describes random quantities by their distributions, and proves what must happen on average and in the long run. This shelf builds the subject in order, from the counting arguments of a first course to the martingales and measure theory of a graduate one. It assumes comfortable algebra, single-variable calculus and a little linear algebra; the measure-theoretic page at the end assumes some real analysis.

Every lesson has a short numpy sample (the outputs quoted are from actual runs), worked problems with hidden solutions, and sources. Several pages have interactive simulations: set the parameters and watch the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem, a Markov chain or a Bayesian update happen.

items: Foundations (#/probability/foundations): sample spaces, the axioms, counting, conditional probability, independence and Bayes' theorem.
Random Variables (#/probability/random-variables): discrete and continuous variables, distribution functions, expectation, variance and moments, and transformations.
Distributions (#/probability/distributions): the standard families (binomial, Poisson, exponential, gamma, normal, beta, chi-square, t) and how they are related.
Several Random Variables (#/probability/multivariate): joint and conditional distributions, covariance and correlation, conditional expectation, sums and convolutions, and the multivariate normal.
Tools (#/probability/toolkit): generating functions, the classical inequalities, and entropy.
Limit Theorems (#/probability/limit-theorems): modes of convergence, the laws of large numbers, the central limit theorem and Monte Carlo methods.
Random Processes (#/probability/processes): Markov chains, random walks and martingales, Poisson processes, and Brownian motion.
Inference (#/probability/inference): estimation and maximum likelihood, and Bayesian inference.
Measure-Theoretic Probability (#/probability/measure-theory): σ-algebras, measures, the Lebesgue integral, and conditional expectation done properly.
A first course: Foundations, Random Variables, Distributions, then Covariance and Correlation, The Law of Large Numbers and The Central Limit Theorem.
For machine learning and quantum computing: add Conditional Expectation, The Multivariate Normal, Inequalities, Entropy and Information, Monte Carlo Methods, Markov Chains and both Inference pages.
For a graduate course: everything, with Measure-Theoretic Probability read early as a reference for what the earlier pages take on trust.

blocks.text: Notation used throughout: $P(A)$ for the probability of an event, $X, Y$ for random variables, $E[X]$ for expectation, $\operatorname{Var}(X)$ for variance, $X \sim F$ for 'X has distribution F', and i.i.d. for independent and identically distributed.
